source_title: Brand-New Official $325 PlayStation Release Confirmed for November - GameRant
source_excerpt:
PlayStation is getting a brand-new release that will ship come November and cost fans of the family of consoles $325. While the new launch is pricey, it's already in high demand, so PlayStation fans may not want to wait to check it out.
While the 30th anniversary of the PlayStation was technically in 2024 for Japan and 2025 for the US and Europe, the celebrations surrounding the momentous occasion have continued past that point. The original PlayStation was an entry point to gaming for many, with the system selling over 100 million units and managing to stay in production up until the PS3 released. Fans across numerous generations of the PlayStation family of consoles have been celebrating the anniversary.
A new collectible book called PlayStation: The First 30 Years is releasing in November, with the Deluxe Edition costing a whopping $325. As the title implies, the 400-page book chronicles the history of the PlayStation console, including the behind-the-scenes process of development, much of which has never been seen before by the public. The book is chock-full of PlayStation console concept sketches, R&D prototypes, and models that made it into development but never actually released. While the standard version of the book can be purchased for $125, the Deluxe Edition arrives with an exposed binding, clamshell presentation box, a photographic print signed by Teiyu Goto, who designed the original DualShock controller , and Benedict Redgrove, the book's photographer. As the Deluxe Edition of the book is limited to just 1,994 copies, megafans will need to act quickly in order to grab it from Read Only Memory .
As noted, this book is part of the 30th anniversary celebration of the PlayStation console line, but it's arriving a bit later than expected. PlayStation: The First 30 Years was originally revealed back in 2025 , and had a planned launch of Spring 2026. Expectant fans have been kept waiting, which is likely part of why the pre-orders for the limited Deluxe Edition are selling so quickly. Thankfully, the standard edition of the book has no stated limits on how many copies are available, so fans who miss out on the Deluxe Edition can still pick it up and enjoy nearly all the same content, and at a lower price.

While many fans are excited about the new book's release and are interested in seeing how their beloved PlayStations were developed, its reception hasn't been entirely positive. Some have expressed frustration at the book's physical release, using it as an opportunity to bring attention to Sony's plan to end physical releases for new games on PlayStation . However, that clearly hasn't stopped fans from buying the book, as the Deluxe Edition's pre-order stock has rapidly depleted.
PlayStation's history hasn't always been smooth, with the PS3 being a notable rough spot for the console brand. While it ultimately succeeded, it didn't manage to achieve anywhere near the sales of its predecessor, the wildly successful PS2. When the 40th anniversary rolls around, it will be interesting to see how the last ten years of PlayStation compare to its first 30.
